summary.intent: Get the RDT-differences documentation PR landed, then assess whether caliper's output is the best it can be for Storybook argTypes mapping and for AI agents, and act on the findings.
summary.outcome: PR #381 (docs/rdt-differences) was opened as a draft with CI pending. An evaluation found caliper's output is on par with Storybook's own docgen in most cases but worse in 17 rows, and lossy for agents. Trail #249 was created with three workers started on projection, TOON and addon handoff fixes, none reported yet.

repo: The Storybook addon (packages/storybook/src/arg-types.ts) converts caliper types into react-docgen-typescript shape and then runs Storybook's own extractArgTypes, so control quality depends on that conversion, not just on resolver accuracy.
The oracle work measured resolver types only and did not measure the Storybook projection step.
Canonical JSON contract changes may require ADR 0017; TOON-only and rdt.rs changes avoid that.

Most of the 17 worse rows are resolver faults already in the oracle trail (opaque keyof/-1, unreduced intersections, 'a'|'b'|string, unbound T, ReturnType kept as a name, unevaluated conditional types). Only three are conversion faults.
The weekly oracle checker text and verdicts come from different TypeScript versions (7.1.0-beta oracle vs TS 6.0.3), and the docs now say so.
Partial/Required/Omit/Pick modifier loss in aliases scores 'less precise' or 'identical', never 'wrong', so the gate does not catch it.
Merge order: #380 (comparator fix) and #381 (doc) should merge together; #379 is independent; resolver fixes wait on #379.

code.finding: type_json emits an enum only for literal unions; everything else gets raw type text as its name, so Storybook shows an object control.
omits() only drops an undocumented children prop, so @ignore props still get controls.
is_literal_union requires at least 2 members, so a single literal like kind?: 'button' falls back to an object control.
incompleteMessages ignores info-level diagnostics, so opaque keyof, -1 and indexed-access types give no warning and the addon still answers.
TOON omits per-prop @deprecated, @see and @since tags (@default is kept); it also truncates unions over 4 members and literal unions over 6 with ...(+N), and drops function parameter names.

friction: Mantine, shadcn, antd and Chakra corpora are not installed locally, so many examples were quoted from the weekly dump rather than reproduced, and the evaluation's corpus rows rest on oracle findings and the worker's own judgement.
The teammate's idle notification was truncated, requiring a follow-up to get the full report.
CI on PRs #379, #380 and #381 was still pending (Entire Gates, Lint, Coverage, etc.), so readiness could not be confirmed.
Class counts (547, 487, 70, etc.) and comparator-artifact counts in the doc were taken from the lead's summary and not re-derived.
open_items: Merge decisions on PRs #379, #380, #381 and #291 are still waiting on the user.
The ReactElement vs reactNode decision is open; the recommendation is to keep reactNode since no evaluated row showed it hurting Storybook.
Results from the three workers on trail #249 (control projection, lossless TOON, addon opaque handoff) have not been seen.
After #380 merges, re-run the oracle on shadcn, spectrum and chakra to confirm wrong drops from 31 to about 3.
After #379 merges, open a trail for the silent-wrong resolver fixes, starting with alias wrappers, plus the opaque, intersection, string-absorbing and unbound-T cases.
Lower-priority items: flag discriminated unions in TOON and keep ReactElement distinct from ReactNode.
Ambient tw augmentation is missing in caliper, and call-signature-only types come out as an empty object; both remain gaps.
